tagline: An old wagon road down to Lake Superior, five falls deep.
intro: Out of Bessemer, among the rock outcrops of the Gogebic Range, County Road 513 runs north through pine, hemlock and hardwood to the mouth of the Black River on Lake Superior. The state had it built as a wagon road by 1904. An 1848 survey map already showed a wagon road running south from the river mouth to the hill where Copper Peak now stands.

The river comes up out of Wisconsin colored by tannin from the hemlocks and drops toward the lake in a series of falls. In the last three miles the byway passes trailheads to five waterfalls: Great Conglomerate, Potawatomi, Gorge, Sandstone and Rainbow.
season: MDOT's byway guide names summer and fall as the best seasons.

moments.title: Copper Peak
moments.text: A hill rising 364 feet beside the road, topped by the only ski-flying jump in the Western Hemisphere. Nobody has flown it since 1994, but a chair lift and elevator still go up.

moments.title: Great Conglomerate Falls
moments.text: A 30-foot fall split around a big conglomerate outcrop in midstream, so that in low summer water it comes down in two drops.

moments.title: Black River Harbor
moments.text: The only harbor in the National Forest System, where a wooden suspension bridge carries the North Country Trail over the river toward Rainbow Falls and the beach.

practical: The Forest Service reports that the waterfall viewing platforms and trails are undergoing major repairs. Most of the waterfall paths have steps.
